content:
Suppose I have a file A.lean with a declaration def foo := some_big_expression which is both public and exposed (e.g. lives in some upstream repo). Now I have a new file B.lean that imports A.lean, but I want foo to be no expose locally in this file B.lean.
Is there a way to achieve this? Thanks!
seal foo (does not affect the kernel though)

Thanks!
Is there a way to also affect kernel? I want to use no expose to improve kernel type checking performance.
I see; unfortunately there is no way to do so currently
There is the @[no_expose] def bar := foo hack.

Sebastian Ullrich said:

I see; unfortunately there is no way to do so currently

Does this mean that under the hood exposed and non exposed defs are treated equally and that exposure "simply" has to do with the higher level module system, establishing what tactics can/cannot access?

Filippo A. E. Nuccio said:

Sebastian Ullrich said:

I see; unfortunately there is no way to do so currently

Does this mean that under the hood exposed and non exposed defs are treated equally and that exposure "simply" has to do with the higher level module system, establishing what tactics can/cannot access?

No, it is just because downstream users cannot change the exposure of a declaration once it is decided in its source module. (The best you can do is create a new declaration wrapping it as suggested above, and control that declaration's exposure.)

Non-exposed and exposed definitions are qualitatively different, as the data for the body of non-exposed declarations is not even loaded downstream. So a non-exposed declaration cannot be unfolded downstream even in principle. (Assuming you don't write import all to insist on importing the private value.)

(What seal does is just change "the degree of unfoldability" of an exposed definition, (only) by changing the transparency settings; the definition is still exposed/unfoldable in principle.)
